source: Time can turn even the most unwilling heart to softness. Time will grow a boy into a man, or a girl into a loving wife.
Such a strange season, this one.
The air becomes thicker with each passing hour.
Y-you... Yer a damn fool.
Are you drunk?
How very like you.
Y'don't even love her.
Brit. Y'don'deserve to be her husband.
That's what this is about? That bloody betrothal?
What are you going on about now?
Yyyer goin' to marry her. H-heard about it from her myself. On account of her father's wishes. But she doesn' want to marry you.
I don't want her either. All she does is sneer. I think she's vile.
What did you call her?
You're a God-damned fool.
Did you come all this way only to tell me that?
You-- You killed him. You'd known him all your life. And still you killed him.
You-- You tried to kill him. You'd known him all your life. And still you tried to kill him.
My father was always good and kind to you, was he not? Was he not the consummate gentleman?
All you've ever done is ruin things. Everything. Everything you touch.
Everyone around you bears the brunt of the hole that threatens to rip you open.
It'd be far better if you— just—
You're right.
It's as I told you before—when I returned your lute to you. You're right. All I do is ruin things.
And now I want to build something, for once.
I need Brit to do that. Neither of us are happy with this arrangement.
You think I don't know you love her?
I want to honor that, Laertes.
I'm sorry about your father. I never meant that night to end as it did. Truly.
And if I could go back and unwind all that transpired, I would.
I am a sick, strange fool, and always shall be. But from now on...
No more of me, Laertes. I shall trouble you and yours no more. This, I promise.
You don't want to do this, Laertes.
I know that face. I've been there many a time.
Go. Leave me, and we'll pretend this never happened.
He would have killed me.
Good riddance.
H-he's dead—
What have I done?
What's wrong?
Your face is so peculiar right now.
He's dead.
He's dead.
What did you do, Laertes?
No. Surely you didn't...
I was angry, and I didn't know what I was doing.
I pushed Hamlet off the walls. Hamlet is dead. I killed him.
Come here, love.
What shall become of us now?
Listen, Laertes. Listen closely to my words.
Your hands are stained with blood. But now that they are, you must stain them once more.
And I know now that you have the courage to do it.
The other nobles, including my father, want Claudius dead. He's a poor King.
In fact, my father asked me to spy on his court and find a way to kill him off.
So you were the spy the King was so concerned about.
Did you try to kill my sister?
Me? Harm your sister? Of course not, love. Just frightened her a little by accident.
Ophelia has such an imaginative quality to her, don't you think?
Of course you would never do my sister harm. I don't know why I suspected you.
(I should've known it was Brit all along.)
(If I move now, she'll only kill me again. I have to find another way.)
I... I am. But trust me, Laertes. I never would have hurt anyone except Claudius.
If you could find it in your heart to use these hands further, then the whole bad tree will be uprooted.
And with all these vile men dead and gone, you and I would linger to love in peace.
There would no longer be anyone to obstruct us. You see?
I'll do it. I'll go to see the King. I'll take his life. It should be me.
Whatever we do now, we do it together. I'll accompany you.
Your hands are stained with blood. That can never be forgotten. But it can be turned into something powerful for us.
The other nobles, including my father, wanted Claudius and Hamlet dead. Claudius was an awful King. His people hated him.
He planned to marry me to Fortinbras. This betrothal to Hamlet was a mere sham. But I never wanted that. You know that to be true.
And with the both of them gone, we can cement my claim to the throne quickly. My father will push through the election in my favor.
I'm going to be Queen of Denmark. And you shall be my King Consort. No one will ever put a stop to me loving you again.
Not now. Not ever. Laertes, this is good for the both of us. We've triumphed.
This is nothing like I thought it would be.
I don't know what to say.
There's no need to fear any longer, my love.
I'll send word to Prince Fortinbras to strike quickly at Elsinore's heart while the castle is weakened.
From there, everything will proceed quickly. You'll see.
You've done right. Sometimes what is right and what is good are at odds.
But make no mistake. This was right. Even if it didn't feel good.
You know what has to be done.
And I came prepared to do it.
He lies down there, asleep in his chamber.
I'll go and do the deed.
What? What's wrong? Is it done?
No. No, it's not done. H-his face is-- it's--
Hush. You'll wake him. Go outside.
If Claudius hadn't resembled my father as he slept, I'd have done it.
I could have. Would have.
I see... a dagger before me, the handle turned towards my hand.
Come, let me clutch it.
I-- I have you not-- and yet I see you still--
This is a false creation. A fatal vision.
Yet I do see you still, and on your blade... gouts of blood.
No. There's no such thing.
While I stand here entertaining this insanity, he lives.
This heated deed must not be cooled.
It's as good as done. I can practically hear the guards ringing the midnight bell.
But you can't hear it, Claudius, can you?
It is a knell. It summons you to Heaven-- or to Hell.
W-who's there?
...Only an owl.
He must be... doing it... right now, surely.
The deed is done. Could you hear any noise?
I heard the owl scream and the crickets cry.
My hands are a sorry sight. Covered in his blood.
That's foolish. Don't call it 'a sorry sight'. We did what we had to.
You mustn't think of what we did. It'll make us mad.
I thought I heard a whisper in there. It cried, 'Sleep no more'. It felt like a curse.
Come. Lift your head. Wash your hands, and I'll wash mine.
My hands are just as bloody as yours, but I'd be ashamed to be carrying on like this.
Let's return to your chambers. A little water will clear away all of this.
Claudius is dead. As it should have been. As it shall now be.
I know what has to be done.
Is this a dagger I see before me? The handle turned towards my hand?
The deed is done.
I thought I heard a whisper, in there. It cried, 'sleep no more.' It felt like a curse.
You told me you were afraid.
I want you to know that I believe you. I believe you're in danger.
But if what you say is true—then you'd better leave the investigation to me.
And why is that?
Because if someone does want to cause you harm, they're watching any moves you make already.
I don't want you caught up in this further.
So... I'm going to turn to someone I trust implicitly.
They have a keen insight into everyone's comings and goings within Elsinore, and might be able to help us narrow down a suspect.
Someone you 'trust?'
And who might that be, exactly?
Just because you're my sister doesn't mean you know all my secrets, you know.
(Hmm. If he won't be honest with me, perhaps I can do some investigation of my own.)
A 'contact'?
You mean Brit.
How did you know?
You're so many wonderful things, Laertes. Subtle is not one of them.
True enough. Yes, Brit's got a knack for understanding the undercurrents in Elsinore, so to speak.
I'll meet with her and understand what I must do from there.
I used to have someone I could trust in times like these.
But she proved herself a liar. So it's just you and me.
Don't tell anyone the things you told me, all right? I wouldn't want this to create a larger panic than it must.
Lady Birgitta, a moment, please.
I need to ask you some questions.
My men have begun a search of your chambers.
Is there anything they might find there which you wish to disclose?
Are you asserting something about me, Guard Captain? Is there some charge you wish to levy on me?
Let us assume charges are forthcoming for the time being.
This must be a mistake. And frankly, the Queen would be livid to know you detained one of her ladies.
This must be a mistake. And frankly, it's embarrassing for you to detain a lady like this.
I do not require the Queen's permission to act in the Crown's best interests.
I do this with the Crown's full permission. Things have changed, Lady Brit.
So I shall ask you just once more. Is there anything you want to tell me, before they find it?
What are you insinuating?
No! There isn't! Leave me alone!
I'm going now. I was just on my way to town.
I am afraid I cannot let you depart the castle.
You are to be detained for the time being.
No! You're not going to put me in that rotten dungeon. You have no proof of anything!
Stop struggling. I can sling you over my shoulder if I must. Or you can take my arm and go quietly.
I owe you an apology.
For what?
I did not believe you. Not at first. Please, come with me.
For putting you in danger until now.
Laertes relayed your fears to me, and at first, I did not believe them. Please, come with me.
See the announcement?

source: All, I bring rather unfortunate news. We have uncovered certain illegitimate activities within the castle which collectively amount to treason.
I apprehended Lady Birgitta earlier today. She is in custody now.
Brit? You're saying she is the one who's been passing information to Norway?
Although you had spoken to us earlier, I still find this distressing beyond belief. I welcomed Lady Brit to this court myself. Are we certain it's true?
I'm afraid so, my lady. And were it not for Lady Ophelia's involvement, we'd never have uncovered the link.
Brit's the one who's been passing information to Norway?
I knew the Brockenhuus family was sympathetic to them, but I didn't expect Brit to be capable of this, truth be told.
I'm afraid so. And were it not for Ophelia's involvement, we'd never have uncovered the link.
She must be punished to the fullest extent, just as any other scoundrel would be.
If that is your wish, my lord. She is in the dungeon now.
